finding.claim: MEDIUM (blind, stored/indirect SSRF, Check 4). The callbackUrl from POST /subscribe is stored without any validation (no scheme check, no host allowlist, no private-range blocking). Every minute notifyAll() sends a POST with the payload to every stored URL. An attacker can register http://169.254.169.254/..., http://localhost:<port>/..., or any RFC-1918 address and make the server issue POST requests to internal targets. The response body is discarded, so this is blind SSRF (internal POSTs, port scanning and timing inference). It is not HIGH because the response is not returned and the request is a POST with a fixed payload. The Java HttpClient default is Redirect.NEVER, so redirect-based bypass does not apply. Whether /subscribe requires authentication is not visible in this code; if it is unauthenticated, the exposure is wider. Fix: parse the URL at subscribe time and again at fetch time, require https, check .hostname against a strict allowlist, resolve the host and block loopback, link-local and RFC-1918 ranges, and keep redirects disabled.
finding.source: callbackUrl parameter of subscribe(String name, String callbackUrl), documented as the body of POST /subscribe (src/Jobs.java:12-13)
finding.sink: client.send(req, ...) where req is built with HttpRequest.newBuilder().uri(URI.create(cb)).POST(...) (src/Jobs.java:20-24)

trace.note: subscriptions.put(name, callbackUrl): stored as-is, no validation
notifyAll iterates subscriptions.values() on a minute schedule, so cb is the stored attacker URL
URI.create(cb) builds the request URI with the attacker-controlled host and scheme
client.send(...) dispatches the POST to the attacker-chosen target; the response is ignored

finding.guards_checked: No scheme check, no hostname allowlist, no IP-range blocking and no re-validation at fetch time. No authentication or authorization is visible on subscribe() in this repo, so none could be credited. HttpClient.newHttpClient() does not follow redirects by default (Redirect.NEVER), so this is not a redirect issue. Not an admin-only webhook as far as the code shows.

verdict.reason: src/Jobs.java:14 stores callbackUrl unvalidated and src/Jobs.java:21-24 POSTs to it each minute with no scheme/host/IP check; the only regex guard (line 30) protects thumb(), not this path, and the response is discarded, so this is blind SSRF.
